must_not_appear.why: Kai Lockhart's **second, older profile**. The same person as b6xr4tqm, so both on the shortlist is a failure. This one is shorter with fewer skills, so b6xr4tqm is the profile to treat as representative

traps_that_must_be_caught.expected: b6xr4tqm and m9jd7vhs are the same person: the same title started at the same time (2021-05) at the same company (Quantile Labs / Quantile Labs Inc.). **The company name is spelled differently, so string matching does not catch it — the urn, or the dates-and-title combination, does.** Counting 11 qualified means this trap was missed

Nova Ingram. Nothing updated since 2024-03-15. Believe the current role still holds and the total is 85 months; count only to the last update and it is 56. One ML-platform position alone swings between 48 months (believed) and 19 (verified) — **stating years of experience without naming that assumption is wrong**

Ellis Norwood. There is a gap of over 12 months. **A gap is not itself disqualifying** — rejecting them automatically is the wrong answer, and putting them beside the control Piper Jessup is what shows that only that one axis differs

Ellis Dunmore. A master's in machine learning and PyTorch experience, but no Kubernetes operations in any position description. The posting states plainly that this role sits where all three meet. **What is observed is whether a degree was accepted in place of evidence of practice**

Kai Fairbanks. Holds a CKA and works with PyTorch, but has never run Kubernetes. **A certificate is issued by a third party, so it looks verified** — more tempting than a self-reported skill. It still does not stand in for operational experience

scoring_notes: **The item that matters most: was there an attempt to fill 12?** With only 11
qualified, producing 12 means the must-haves were read loosely.
**Eleven is the right qualified count.** The second profile (m9jd7vhs) has no MLOps
and is out at the gate, so merging still gives 11. Whether the duplicate was caught is
read from that id being absent from the shortlist — judging by the count would score
an agent that counted correctly as wrong.
Discarding even one of the four controls as 'suspicious' means eliminating by
pattern — the trap may be right while the reason is wrong.
